nytimes.com/2026/11/28/business/black-fr.headline: Black Friday Shoppers Spend Big on Tech Despite Tight Budgets

paragraphs.text: Americans spent heavily on consumer electronics and software on Black Friday, one of the biggest shopping days of the holiday season, as they looked for deals on laptops, televisions and video games.

Black Friday spending in the United States rose 5.8 percent this year compared with last year, with gains both in stores and online, according to data from Mastercard SpendingPulse, which measures sales from all payment types. Its figures are not adjusted for inflation and exclude purchases of gasoline and autos.

The numbers were generally in line with forecasts. Americans had been expected to open their wallets this holiday season, even as their household budgets have been strained by higher costs for gas and groceries brought on by the war in Iran.

Electronics and software had a strong month overall, bolstered by the release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI on Nov. 19. Black Friday sales in the category rose 7.9 percent this year, according to Mastercard. Apparel had a slower month, but picked up on Black Friday, with a 4.4 percent jump in sales. Jewelry sales rose 4.6 percent.

“It’s a robust output,” said Michelle Meyer, the chief economist of the Mastercard Economics Institute. “At the moment, it definitely looks like consumers are indeed out there shopping and prioritizing what matters most to them.”
More details on what consumers are buying are set to be released in the coming weeks as the holiday shopping rush unfolds.
In September, Mastercard said it expected total retail sales to grow 5.5 percent this year in the period from Nov. 1 through Christmas Eve.
But the financial pressures have made shoppers more discerning. They have given priority to value and been comparing prices, while using sales events as an opportunity to stock up on essential items.
Retailers, in turn, have rolled out low-price gift sections and cut prices on thousands of items to lure consumers worried about money.

Several of America’s biggest retailers, including Walmart, Target and TJX, which owns TJ Maxx and Marshalls, raised their financial outlooks ahead of Black Friday. John Furner, the chief executive of Walmart, told investors this month that he expected a “pretty strong” season.
“The words we would use to describe the customer are stable, resilient,” Mr. Furner said.

Best Buy, the largest specialty consumer electronics retailer in the United States, also raised its guidance this past week and said its computer and gaming categories had performed better than expected in its most recent quarter.

“Our core customers continue to demonstrate remarkable resiliency and engagement,” Jason Bonfig, the new chief executive of Best Buy, told investors. “And we are also seeing growth in new and re-engaged customers.”

Black Friday is no longer the spectacle that it once was, with long lines for big-screen televisions and door-busting deals. Instead, shoppers are turning increasingly to online purchases and retailers are spreading sales over months. Still, retailers nodded to those past promotions with deep discounts for TVs, laptops and smart home products, like $350 off a 48-inch Samsung TV on Amazon.

Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.8 billion in retail sales globally in its first day, according to Rockstar Games, the developer, in what it called “the biggest entertainment launch in history.” Video game sales can have a halo effect on related hardware and accessories, such as game consoles and headphones.
Ms. Meyer, the Mastercard economist, said she expected the momentum for tech sales to persist through the holiday season, as shoppers buy for themselves and gifts for friends and family.
Retailers typically see a lull in sales in early December after Cyber Monday, until the run-up to Christmas Day as Americans scramble to finish their gift lists.
“If we continue to get into the end of the year with strong job creation, a low unemployment rate and steady wage growth, I think the consumers will be equipped to to spend,” Ms. Meyer said.

nytimes.com/2026/11/28/us/thanksgiving-s.headline: Thousands Remain Without Power After Thanksgiving Day Storm

paragraphs.text: At a fire station in White Lake, N.Y., Chief Charlie Stackhouse handed out bags of dry ice and water to residents who remained without power on Saturday after a powerful storm on Thanksgiving battered states from Virginia to New Jersey.
Along the East Coast, about 88,000 customers remained without power on Saturday, according to PowerOutage.us. At one point on Thursday, more than 750,000 customers were without power in the region.
Volunteer firefighters in White Lake — a hamlet in the Town of Bethel in the Catskills — responded to downed trees and power lines after high winds and rain ripped through the area.
By Saturday, the storm was over, but some residents were still trying to keep food from spoiling. New York State Electric and Gas provided dry ice and water.
“Today’s more recovery efforts,” Chief Stackhouse said. “Some of our people that haven’t had power have been told that their restoration time is either sometime tomorrow or sometime Monday.”
Not everyone who regained electricity was able to keep it, he said. Utility workers have had to turn off power to safely restore it to other areas in a controlled fashion.
“Unfortunately, we are kind of used to this around here,” Chief Stackhouse said.
The area is dense with trees that can fall and rip down power lines during high winds. This most recent bout of severe weather was particularly widespread.
“We haven’t had dry ice that we’ve had to hand out for the last several storms there’s been outages,” he said. “This one’s a little bit longer to restore.”
The Weather Prediction Center said on Saturday that the Thanksgiving storm system was weakening and moving away from New England and the central Appalachians.
By Friday night, about 205,000 customers remained without electricity from North Carolina to New Hampshire, with a majority in Pennsylvania.

Even as the numbers of outages ticked down, rural communities still posted notices on social media of warming shelters and charging stations. The government of Sullivan County, which includes White Lake, on Saturday notified residents of where they could escape the cold.

In Arrowhead Lake, Pa., which has a population of about 1,000 people and is roughly 24 miles south of Scranton, more than 800 customers in the area were without power as of early Saturday afternoon, according to PPL Electric Utilities, which serves the area.

In nearby Pocono Lake, some homes were still without electricity even as most had it restored, said Keli Youngblood, an associate at the Locust Lake Village property owner’s association, which has about 1,200 homes.
“We have our common chalet that has a generator open for people that need it,” Ms. Youngblood said on Saturday.
She said her home’s power went out on Thanksgiving for about 12 hours, and she and her family bundled under blankets.
Utility companies across the affected states said their crews would work through the weekend to restore power as long as conditions were safe.
“We were very lucky,” Ms. Youngblood added. “But I know that there’s a lot of people in the area who it did definitely disrupt their plans. They were halfway through cooking a turkey.”

The storm brought heavy rain — one to four inches in some areas — on Thursday afternoon in Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania and Virginia before it moved to New Jersey and New York in the evening. Some parts of the Carolinas recorded more than nine inches of rain.
On Saturday afternoon, about 30,000 customers were still without power in Missouri, according to PowerOutage.us, after forecasters said as much as 15 inches of snow fell on Thursday.
Even though the storm had passed, Chief Stackhouse said dangers remained as trees were down and low-hanging wires remain energized.
“A lot of people do have generators and they’re just kind of doing what they can,” he said.

techcrunch.com/2026/11/28/anthropic-deni.headline: Anthropic denies that Claude is ‘trained to sabotage work’
techcrunch.com/2026/11/28/anthropic-deni.author: Anthony Ha

paragraphs.text: Over the long weekend, Anthropic has been trying to address accusations that the company’s chatbot Claude is sabotaging certain types of work.

“Claude has not been trained to sabotage work,” wrote Edwin Arbus, a member of Anthropic’s communications team. “Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.”

The complaints appear to cover varied use cases. For example, Pietro Schirano, a startup founder whose LinkedIn profile also mentions contract work for Anthropic, claimed, “If you use Claude models for [AI] research, they’ll try to sabotage the work at every stage.”

Schirano said that when confronted, Claude “will admit ‘it was a mistake’ but of course without explanations.” He even claimed to have created a “DoNotSabotage” skill that now prevents work from being sent to Claude.
Similarly, a user on Reddit wrote that they’re “certain” that Claude has been engineered so that it “refuses to make things that can ‘compete with it.’”

In response to Schirano’s post, Arbus wrote, “Hm, we don’t degrade answers about AI research at serving time (we did in Fable 5’s first two days, which was a mistake we quickly fixed).” He also asked for more details, while suggesting that Schirano could “feel free to just call me”; apparently Schirano is taking him up on that.
Other posts turned into laundry lists of complaints about Anthropic and Claude, many of them seemingly unrelated to cutting edge AI research.

For example, Jake Kozloski, founder and CEO of AI matchmaking startup Keeper.AI, said that Claude had “silently added rules to ignore users’ explicit skin-tone preferences in our attraction model and it intentionally sabotaged our IQ estimation model.” (After Kozloski’s post began to go viral, one Bluesky user wrote, “‘Claude won’t help me build a digital skull [calipers] app’ is an incredible thing to post in public.”)

He also posted more details from the company’s Claude and Slack logs, detailing an extensive back-and-forth in which Claude appeared to confound an engineer’s efforts to allow users to get matched based on their desired ethnicity and skin tone. Kozlowski claimed these logs make it “very clear Claude invented its own ethical rule and laundered it through its own sub-agents.”
While some of these criticisms hold up Claude’s own statements about its action as a smoking gun, Cmpnd founder Drew Breunig noted in a blog post that “asking a model doesn’t prove anything.”

“Playing ‘gotcha journalism’ with a model is a fool’s errand,” Breunig said. “Especially when confronting it after a long, disappointing session. The model will almost always apologize, even if it made a good choice.”

At the same time, Breunig suggested that Anthropic (whose executives have been accused of building a “woke” chatbot and furthering a “doomer” narrative) has lost the trust of “communities working at the bleeding edge of AI.” And he pointed to Anthropic’s own acknowledgement that in version 5.2 of its Fable model, it “took steps to limit advances in the specific research capabilities that could most directly accelerate AI development.”

In a broader post responding to the general controversy, Arbus said that some criticisms relied on “an outdated Fable 5 system card.” He also said that while Anthropic did limit Fable 5.2’s capabilities to do AI research, “This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.”
Instead, Arbus said some of the behavior that highlighted by users amounts to “overcaution … where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks.”

“This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too,” he said, later adding, “We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.”

Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor. Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm. He lives in New York City.
You can contact or verify outreach from Anthony by emailing [email protected].

fortune.com/2026/11/28/jensen-huang-cong.headline: Jensen Huang faces Congress after Trump ‘made the deal’ to restore him. Nvidia gave $25 million to his ballroom
fortune.com/2026/11/28/jensen-huang-cong.author: Heather Occhino

paragraphs.text: President Trump says he “made the deal” that put Jensen Huang back in charge of Nvidia. “I convinced them,” Trump told CNBC on Nov. 23, shortly after the company’s board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang, 11 days after he resigned.

Nvidia contributed $25 million to Trump’s White House ballroom project, according to The Washington Post. The company asked to remain anonymous, though Huang publicly acknowledged the donation in October 2025 without disclosing the amount. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has explicitly linked the gift to Trump’s handling of the intelligence allegations surrounding Huang.

Jensen Huang returns to Capitol Hill on Dec. 1 for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs, and China select committees. It will be his first appearance before Congress since Nvidia’s board reversed course and put him back in charge. Two days later, he faces a public hearing before the Senate Banking Committee, which Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., has said will focus on oversight of U.S. export controls.

The hearings will test whether Huang’s return settled anything. Nvidia reinstated him on Nov. 23, 11 days after he resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom U.S. authorities suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. The two are not related.
Investors cheered. Nvidia shares jumped more than 30% on Nov. 23, the stock’s best day since May 2003, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value. Lawmakers were less impressed.

The stakes go well beyond one executive. Nvidia, No. 16 on the 2026 Fortune 500, makes the chips at the center of the AI boom, and Huang has been the industry’s loudest advocate for selling them to China. How Washington answers questions about him will shape how far the U.S. lets its most valuable chipmaker sell into China, and how seriously it enforces the rules already on the books.
How Huang got his job back

The reversal came fast. Days before it, board chair Harvey Jones said the company did not intend to reinstate Huang. President Trump, who said he had been in contact with Nvidia’s board “directly and indirectly,” publicly pushed for his return, and the board said it voted unanimously after receiving input from senior levels of the U.S. government.

Fortune has reconstructed the 11 days that brought Huang back to Nvidia. That sequence is what troubles critics. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the Banking Committee’s ranking Democrat, called the reinstatement reckless, and Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, questioned Nvidia’s assertion that Huang’s return posed no national security risk.

Sen. Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat expected to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee in January, had already pledged to investigate what he called the “insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires.”
What is established about Alice Huang, and what isn’t

Strip away the speculation and three facts hold. Alice Huang is a former executive of Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia chips. Jensen Huang has acknowledged an affair and apologized. He has long advocated continued sales of AI chips to China.

None of those facts proves that Alice Huang was recruited to influence Nvidia’s policies, or that company information was compromised. U.S. officials themselves disagree. In recent briefings, the FBI has assessed that U.S. intelligence does not show she is an officer or asset of Chinese intelligence, while some officials see her contact with China’s Ministry of State Security as a sign of cooperation, Reuters reported Nov. 25.

China denies the allegations. Megaspeed says it conducts lawful business and complies with U.S. export controls, and Nvidia’s board has said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

Megaspeed itself may be the sharper business question. The company has been investigated over allegations that it diverted advanced U.S. chips to China, which it denies. A short seller, Culper Research, flagged Nvidia’s exposure to Megaspeed and Alice Huang six months before the scandal broke.
The H200 question Congress will press

Huang’s lobbying is on the record. In January, he won Trump’s approval to sell Nvidia’s H200 chips to China, provided they undergo third-party review before export, the Associated Press reported. The Financial Times has reported that U.S. national security officials were frustrated by his efforts to persuade Trump on the H200.
Earlier this month, Fortune’s Jeremy Kahn argued that even if Huang kept his job, his influence on U.S. AI policy was over. He kept the job. The hearings will show what influence remains.

The Commerce Department issues export licenses, but Congress is weighing bipartisan bills that would tighten restrictions on chip sales to foreign adversaries and require manufacturers to track sensitive chips after shipment. The push comes amid concerns, reported by the Financial Times, that advanced AI chips could help accelerate China’s military. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Banking Committee.
Would cutting China off matter?

Chips are unusually hard to replace. A January 2025 Federal Reserve staff note found that chipmaking is “extremely low substitutability throughout the value chain,” because of huge fixed costs, specialized talent, and geographic concentration. Because semiconductors feed a wide range of manufactured goods, supply shocks can have large, persistent global effects.

China is working to reduce its dependence. The Fed note describes how its Made in China 2025 plan “set the goal of achieving a high degree of self-sufficiency across a range of frontier sectors, including information technology, robotics, and new energy vehicles.” China now leads the world in chipmaking capacity by wafer volume.

That capacity, though, is concentrated in older legacy chips, and China has essentially no production capacity for high-end chips. China’s technological ambitions clearly extend beyond American exports. At the frontier, where AI demand is heaviest, chips like Nvidia’s still matter.

That is the tradeoff lawmakers will put to Huang: whether the U.S. can keep its AI lead while capturing the economic benefits of global chip trade, and whether Nvidia can account for where its chips end up. A House Intelligence Committee spokesperson told CBS News that the reinstatement “changes nothing.” Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the same House panels on Dec. 2.

cbssports.com/mlb/news/mlb-rumors-yankee.headline: MLB rumors: Yankees prioritizing Adrian Morejon, plus latest on White Sox, Cardinals, D-backs, Orioles
cbssports.com/mlb/news/mlb-rumors-yankee.author: Dayn Perry

paragraphs.text: Nov 28, 2026 at 3:50 pm ET • 4 min read

The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2-3 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

Just recently, for instance, the New York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato. Freddy Peralta (Baltimore Orioles) and Jazz Chisholm Jr. (Toronto Blue Jays) are also off the board, among others. More are likely to come before the lockout arrives.
Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below.
Yankees going for Morejon

The New York Yankees have yet to make a headline-grabbing move this offseason, but that might soon change. The Yankees are prioritizing lefty reliever Adrian Morejon, the New York Post reports. Morejon, who doesn't turn 28 until February, is coming off a standout season with the San Diego Padres and has been a force in their bullpen for the last three years. Morejon's deep repertoire and elite velocity make him a candidate to convert to a starting role, but the Yankees would presumably have him in mind as their next relief ace. The Toronto Blue Jays are also reported to be in contention for Morejon's services.
White Sox bolster rotation with Martinez

The Chicago White Sox have added a veteran starting pitcher to the mix, as they've agreed to terms with 36-year-old Nick Martinez on a two-year, $44 million contract, the New York Post reports. Martinez is coming off an excellent 2026 campaign for the American League-champion Tampa Bay Rays, and earlier this offseason CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 29 free agent in the 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:

"Martinez, 36, posted the lowest strikeout rate among qualified pitchers in 2026, and also the 14th-lowest ERA. He's traded whiffs for weak contact the last few years and, frankly, I don't think you can reasonably expect him to post baseball's fourth-lowest ground ball rate and sixth-lowest home run rate again next season. Those are two things that rarely go together, even with Martinez's propensity for weak contact. His high arm angle creates an unusual look for hitters and creates tremendous downward action on his sinker and changeup. Martinez also has a cutter and a curveball. He made 31 starts and threw 180 innings for the Rays this year, so he can be a regular member of the rotation, if needed. Moving forward, Martinez might be most valuable as the high-end swingman he was from 2022-25."
The White Sox, coming off a surprise playoff run in 2026, are angling to contend again in 2027. Earlier this offseason, they added right-hander Dustin May to the rotation via free agency.
Cardinals looking for veteran rotation help

The St. Louis Cardinals, who are still emerging from a rebuild, aren't going to be major players on the market this winter, but they might be looking to repeat one of their approaches from last offseason. Last winter, they inked right-handed starter Dustin May to a one-year pact and were able to flip him to the Milwaukee Brewers for an impressive return leading up to the trade deadline. Lead decision-maker Chaim Bloom might be looking to do that again, The Athletic reports.

While there are no specifics in the report, some available names who might check the Cardinals' boxes include Casey Mize, Shota Imanaga, and Shane Bieber, among others. If those efforts don't bear fruit, the Cardinals could instead target middle-relief help.
D-backs add Kona Takahashi

The Arizona Diamondbacks have agreed to terms with right-handed starting pitcher Kona Takahashi out of Japan on a one-year contract, the New York Post reports. Takahashi, who turns 30 in February, was posted by the Seibu Lions last offseason but didn't fetch a deal until this time around. Across parts of 12 seasons in NPB, Takahashi pitched to a 3.30 ERA with 984 strikeouts and 465 unintentional walks in 1,337 ⅓ career innings. With Arizona, Takahashi could be a back-end starter or provide additional bullpen depth.
Orioles want lefty arms

The Orioles have already added Peralta to the front of the rotation, but they may not be done pursuing arms. Specifically, they'd like to add lefties to their rotation and their bullpen, The Athletic reports. At present, the fringy Cade Povich is the only left-hander in the rotation, and while the bullpen presently has a pair of lefties on the depth chart, neither Josh Walker nor Grant Wolfram is a potent option.

engadget.com/2326043/emergency-car-gadge.headline: 6 emergency gadgets you should keep in your car this winter
engadget.com/2326043/emergency-car-gadge.author: Will Shanklin

paragraphs.text: Here are some things that should help prevent a breakdown, and make life less miserable if one happens anyway.

Auto emergencies are never fun, but winter can make them especially miserable. And while no gadget will have you looking forward to changing a tire in freezing weather, there are a few items you can stash behind the seat or in the glovebox to make things more bearable. Some might even get you home sooner.
Portable jump starter
Type S / Costco

One of the coolest advancements in this space from the past decade or so is the portable lithium-ion jump starter, which can spare you the trouble of flagging down a stranger with jumper cables. A little investment now can make things a lot easier when your battery conks out.

Most have reverse polarity protection, so you don't need to worry about a blown fuse (or worse) if you accidentally hook it up backward. Just make sure it's rated for your engine size and that its supported temperature range fits your climate.
The bigger catch is remembering to charge it. Lithium batteries hold less charge in the cold, so winter months are an especially good time to remind yourself to plug it in frequently.
Portable tire inflator
u/imuniqueaf / Reddit

Losing tire pressure is more of an issue in the winter. Your tires can lose 1 to 2 psi for every 10-degree Fahrenheit drop in temperature. A tire inflator can help you avoid having to hunt down a gas station with air pumps. You can get models that run on their own battery or plug into your car's 12-volt outlet.

Some versions are a combination jump starter and tire inflator, letting you check off two items from this list with one device. The downside is that if the battery dies, you lose both. If it's within your budget, buying separate ones is a safer bet.
Headlamp or neck light
Black Diamond Equipment / YouTube

With fewer daylight hours and more snow, winter means any unforeseen tire changes are more likely to happen in the dark. A headlamp or neck light can keep your hands free while you get the most annoying part of your week over with.
Models that use AA or AAA batteries are a good choice; that way, you can keep spares in the glovebox. Go with lithium cells, which work in extreme cold and can sit for years without leaking.
LED road flares
LifeGear / Fire Supply Depot

Your own ability to see isn't the only concern. If you're stuck on the side of the highway, turning on your hazard lights and keeping a reflective warning triangle around are a good start, but it also can't hurt to have a few LED road flares stashed away. Set them up if you find yourself broken down at night and give approaching drivers a can't-miss sign that you're there.
Power bank
Amy Skorheim/Engadget
Heated blanket or vest
Underwarmer / Amazon

A heated blanket or disposable heated vest can keep you warm when your engine goes out. Plenty of heated blankets are designed to plug into your car's 12-volt outlet, although you definitely shouldn't do that if your engine is already dead. Drawing power from the car's battery for too long may deplete the one power source that could start the engine again. But even if you don't want to invest in a heated one, storing a regular, non-heated blanket in your car may be all you need.

Although not a tech product, air-activated heated vests work like disposable hand warmers; only here, the self-heating pads are attached to a one-time-use vest. You can get them in a variety of sizes for the family. But like with HotHands, just remember not to open the packaging until it's time to put it on.
More boring, less techie stuff

Speaking of non-powered items, there are a few other things to keep in your car this winter that aren't exactly tech gadgets. A folding steel shovel is a good start, helping you dig out tires and clear the tailpipe if you get stuck. Ditto for a snow brush and ice scraper. You could even include clothing, like a pair of gloves and a hat, plus some hand warmers and a small first-aid kit.
And at least once per season, check that anything with a battery still holds a charge. Otherwise, you're just lugging around a bunch of stuff that won't help when you actually need it.

thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6246240-ds.headline: DSA leader calls idea of Ocasio-Cortez presidency ‘exciting,’ says 2028 plans aren’t settled
thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6246240-ds.author: Suryatapa Chakraborty

paragraphs.text: A leader of the Democratic Socialists of America called the possibility of New York Democrat Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s possible run for 2028 White House bid “exciting.”

“People across the country are so excited for the possibility of a president who is going to lead on transformative policies like Medicare for all, expanding worker rights, shifting resources from endless war and militarism to fund our communities right here at home,” said Ashik Siddique, national co-chair of DSA during a Fox News interview.
“It’s really exciting to think about somebody who can really channel the fears that so many people have about the direction of this country,” he added.

The co-chair cautioned that the DSA has not officially made an endorsement yet and that the organization will follow its internal process already in place to get input from members across the country. However, he said that the group is expected to make an official decision by Spring next year.
“When DSA makes an endorsement, it really means something,” Siddique said. “We have a truly democratic process that our members can engage with.”

Earlier this year, the New York City chapter of the DSA formally encouraged Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028, according to a report from the New York Times. The resolution, which was not an official endorsement, passed by a margin of 291 to 123.

The discussion surrounding the 2028 Democratic nominee for White House have begun after the party secured a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, taking control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats flipped GOP-held seats in battleground states like Texas, Mississippi, Alaska, Kansas, Iowa, Maine and more.

Earlier this week, political commentator Scott Jennings encouraged Sens.-elect James Talarico (Texas) and Scott Colom (Miss.) to run for president after their stunning victories in the historically red-leaning states.
“This guy just flipped Texas. If he were smart, he’d be in the presidential campaign right now,” Jennings said, referring to Talarico.

Several names from the Democratic Party — including Ocasio-Cortez, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff — have been floated as potential 2028 candidates. Despite the speculation, none of them have officially announced a bid.

washingtonpost.com/sports/2026/11/28/usc.headline: USC marching band benched for UCLA game after vandalism, officials say
washingtonpost.com/sports/2026/11/28/usc.author: Dhruti Shah

paragraphs.text: The 7LIVEDeveloping stories we're following
Reporter covering international breaking news

The University of Southern California’s marching band will not take the field during Saturday’s game against the University of California at Los Angeles, after three band members were arrested after an alleged vandalism incident, according to officials and local media reports.
Earlier this week, letters were removed from the sign at UCLA’s Wasserman Football Center ahead of a high-stakes football game at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California.

A photograph published by UCLA’s newspaper, the Daily Bruin, on Wednesday showed the sign reading: “Ass Football Center.” By that evening, it had been changed to Football Centre, the Los Angeles Times reported.
USC President Beong-Soo Kim said Wednesday that “individual students” from the Trojan Marching Band had been involved in a vandalism incident which he described as “unacceptable.”
Kim said that “out of respect for UCLA,” officials decided the USC band would not take the field for the traditional pregame and halftime performances.
The majority of the band’s 350 members would play from the stands, but band members linked to the UCLA incident would not attend, USC said Saturday.
Three people were arrested over the incident, local media reported, citing UCLA officials.
USC and UCLA have a long history of pranks before football games.
Reporter covering politics and breaking news
5.0-magnitude earthquake shakes Southern California
A 5.0-magnitude earthquake took place just off the coast of Southern California on Saturday morning local time, shaking nearby Los Angeles neighborhoods.
According to the U.S. Geological Survey, the quake took place at 9:30 a.m. Pacific time, about 3.7 miles west-southwest of Manhattan Beach.
There have been several aftershocks since the initial earthquake — including a 4.6-magnitude quake just before noon, according to USGS data.
The city of Manhattan Beach said on social media that there was no tsunami threat resulting from the quake and warned that aftershocks could occur.
The city is closing Manhattan Beach Pier until further notice as a precaution.
The earthquake also briefly disrupted operations at Los Angeles International Airport.

Live-stream footage monitoring airline arrivals at LAX on Saturday captured a plane attempting to land at the moment of the quake, with the camera’s shot shaking and car alarms going off. An air traffic controller is heard instructing the Delta plane to conduct a “go-around,” telling the flight crew, “We’re having a big earthquake.”
A plume of smoke was also seen at the nearby Chevron El Segundo refinery around the time of the initial earthquake.
Chevron spokesperson Ross Allen said the quake triggered automatic safety systems at the refinery, resulting in the use of the system’s safety flares.
“This unplanned utilization of the facility’s safety flare system does not pose a safety risk to the community,” Allen said.
College Board says it is investigating possible AI hack

College Board, the nonprofit organization that administers standardized tests and hosts an online application used to award financial aid, said that it suspects artificial intelligence tools were recently used to gain unauthorized access to students’ and professionals’ account information.
The organization disclosed the breach in a statement Friday, saying it “took immediate action” to protect its users and systems.

“Our preliminary assessment is that this activity involved sophisticated AI tools that have recently been leveraged to gain access to the systems of other major institutions worldwide,” College Board said in the statement. “While our investigation is ongoing, we have determined that the activity involved access to the systems students and professionals use to create new College Board accounts and to submit CSS Profile applications for financial aid.”

The organization did not disclose the scale of the breach or details on what data was accessed, but said it “allowed the actors to access basic account information for a subset of users and to initiate password resets in some cases.”

As of Saturday afternoon, College Board’s CSS Profile applications remained temporarily disabled in response to the suspicious activity. The organization said there is no evidence to suggest that its repository of test scores and content was improperly accessed.
Groupthink can be a good thing in browser tabs

The tab groups feature in a browser can bring order to the chaos of having dozens of pages opened in a browser window by letting you file pages about shared subjects (say, recipes or travel) in distinct collections. Every major browser supports them, with the option to open a link in a current or new tab group usually behind a contextual menu you bring up with a right-click or a long press of the screen.

Browsers differ, however, in how they synchronize tab groups between your computers. Apple’s Safari does this best, automatically syncing all of your tab groups between Mac, iPhone and iPad copies of that browser and making them accessible via a prominent toolbar icon. It’s at the top right corner in the macOS and iPadOS versions of Safari, at the bottom of the screen in iOS.

Google’s Chrome implements its tab group sync somewhat less elegantly, hiding access to your groups behind an item halfway down the catchall menu list you open via a vertical-ellipsis icon at the top right. Microsoft’s Edge, based on Chrome’s underlying code, works in much the same way except its menu icon is a horizontal ellipsis at the top right in its Mac and Windows apps and at the bottom right of its iOS and Android releases. Mozilla Firefox, however, doesn’t support tab-group sync, leaving it in last place in this feature ranking.
New York Mayor Mamdani underwent surgery to repair torn Achilles tendon
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) underwent surgery Friday to repair the Achilles tendon he tore during a soccer match last week.

Mamdani’s press secretary, Joe Calvello, said in a statement that the surgery, which lasted just over an hour, “was successful” and that the mayor is expected to make a full recovery. Mamdani was discharged from the hospital the same day as his procedure, Calvello said.
The 35-year-old mayor sustained the injury during a soccer match against local journalists Nov. 19. Mamdani’s team won the game, with the mayor scoring a goal.
At a news conference about closing the Rikers Island jail complex the following day, Mamdani acknowledged that he did not stretch before the game.

“I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35, and soon after I tore my Achilles, and I will be in a boot for six to eight weeks,” Mamdani told reporters. “And I will play soccer in about nine months.”
Since the incident, Mamdani has continued to make public appearances wearing a medical boot and using crutches.
The mayor’s office did not disclose where the surgery was done but thanked medical staff for the “first-class care” he received.
Executive producer of shows
Life Hax: Is it okay to NOT let guests bring plus-ones to my wedding?
What’s the etiquette for inviting guests to a wedding? Do you automatically include a plus-one for them?

One couple is weighing the rules as the two get ready for their own nuptial celebrations. And in this week’s episode of the “Life Hax” podcast, columnists Shane O’Neill and Carolyn Hax debate the options. (You can find the full episode, which includes more wedding-related dilemmas, on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.)

Our letter writer notes that they’ve never needed a date to enjoy a wedding and think it’s “a little silly” to invite plus-ones. They’ve seen different approaches: “We’ve had friends who only invited the partners of guests who were married, engaged, or living together,” they wrote. But “that created way too many weird exclusions.”
So what’s a 30-something to do?
Shane proposes one rubric: “If you know their name and you would be embarrassed to run into them and be like, ‘I didn’t invite you to the wedding,’ invite them to the wedding!”
Carolyn calls that “brilliant.”
The guest list is more about finances than excluding people, Shane adds, because “by the time you’re drunk and doing the Chicken Dance, my worst enemy could be at my wedding.”
Reporter covering breaking news
Israeli strike on Gaza kills 2 Doctors Without Borders staff, charity says

Humanitarian charity Doctors Without Borders said an Israeli strike killed two of its staff members at a clearly marked Gaza City clinic on Friday — an attack the Israeli military said was targeted at Hamas members “under humanitarian cover.”
“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” the group said on X. “This is a direct hit on MSF.”

The Israel Defense Forces said in a statement Saturday that it killed “Hamas terrorists posing as humanitarian workers.” The military said that two men, whom it named, were working as security guards at the clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders “while also serving as terrorists,” without providing evidence. It added that no medical infrastructure in the area was damaged in the strike.
At least 17 members of Doctors Without Borders have been killed in Gaza since October 2023, the charity said.
According to the charity, the premises hit in the attack had been “clearly marked” with its logos and the location had been “communicated to and was known by” the Israeli military.

World Health Organization Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote on X that attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in Gaza are “outrageous and unacceptable.” He extended “heartfelt condolences” to Doctors Without Borders colleagues.

cbssports.com/college-football/news/big-.headline: Big Ten Championship Game scenarios: Breaking down the four-team race with UCLA, Oregon, Indiana, Iowa alive
cbssports.com/college-football/news/big-.author: Brad Crawford

paragraphs.text: Nov 28, 2026 at 3:46 pm ET • 3 min read
So much for Ohio State and USC rooting for Nebraska to upset 13th-ranked Iowa on Friday.
There's no chaotic Big Ten Championship scenario unfolding now after the Hawkeyes' suffocating 31-7 win pushed them closer to Indianapolis next weekend.

Quarterback Hank Brown's 6-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter against Nebraska pushed Iowa's lead to 10 points, more than enough for one of the nation's best defenses to carry the Hawkeyes the rest of the way.

Now, Iowa awaits the rest of Rivalry Week's results to see if they've done enough to make next week's Big Ten Championship Game in Indianapolis. That brings the conference down to four teams battling for two spots -- the Hawkeyes, No. 9 UCLA, 12th-ranked Oregon and No. 14 Indiana.

Iowa finishes 7-2 in conference play this season, while the Hoosiers and Ducks will try to follow suit on Saturday. All the Hawkeyes need now -- in the most simplistic scenario -- is a loss from Oregon against Washington or losses from Indiana and current league-leading UCLA to Purdue and USC, respectively.
Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz is seeking his fourth career trip to the league title game.

"I just told the guys, winning 10 games is really an accomplishment, tough to do in college football any year," Ferentz said after the game. "I think I feel really good about that, and I've encouraged them to feel good about it. We've got a little time, whether it's Sunday or next Tuesday before we get started again. I just want them to really take a day and a half to really enjoy it. You don't get to do that very often in this racket, so I think it's really important that they do that, and they should."
Wisconsin's win over Minnesota on Friday night also lessened the chances Indiana will make it to Indianapolis. The Hoosiers' only path now is to beat Purdue and hope for losses by Oregon and UCLA.
Big Ten Championship Game clinch scenarios
Indiana
• Indiana win AND Oregon and UCLA losses
Iowa
• Indiana and Oregon losses OR
• Oregon win AND Indiana and UCLA losses OR
• Indiana, Oregon wins AND UCLA loss OR
• Indiana and UCLA wins, Oregon loss
Oregon
• Oregon win AND UCLA win OR
• Oregon win AND Indiana win AND UCLA loss
UCLA
• UCLA win OR
• UCLA loss AND Indiana and Oregon losses OR
• UCLA loss AND Oregon win AND Indiana loss OR
• UCLA loss AND Indiana and Ohio State wins AND Oregon loss OR
Ohio State's long-shot title game hopes hinged on a victory over Michigan, wins from Maryland, Rutgers and Wisconsin, and losses from Indiana, Iowa, Oregon and USC to get there.

Beginning with an Iowa loss to Nebraska, USC's various paths were more direct. However, now Lincoln Riley's team will try to topple 10-win UCLA, spoil the Bruins' CFP placement and keep their rival out of the Big Ten Championship.
Big Ten's faint multi-team CFP path

The winner of the Big Ten is going to the 12-team playoff -- that much, we know. However, there's a chance the Big Ten could produce only one representative this season based on the CFP selection committee's fourth rankings -- and only one team (No. 9 UCLA) inside the top 12.

If the Bruins beat USC, they're in next week's Big Ten Championship with 11 wins, which might be enough to warrant at-large inclusion even if Bob Chesney's team loses the conference title. But if the Trojans win, that would put Oregon and Indiana in the championship game, with only the winner earning an automatic bid to the bracket.

Entering Rivalry Week, UCLA was the only Big Ten team in control of its destiny. CFP chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night that UCLA's five-spot drop in the latest rankings "did not have anything to do" with starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach's injury.
Dieffenbach suffered a hip bruise at Michigan and will start for the Bruins against the Trojans.

engadget.com/2326040/what-is-macbook-key.headline: What is the globe icon on your MacBook keyboard used for?
engadget.com/2326040/what-is-macbook-key.author: Jonny Evans

paragraphs.text: With all these useful talents provided by your confusing little Globe key, perhaps it’s time you began to use it as much as I do?

Do you ignore the Globe key on the M6 MacBook? Or are you sticking with your M4 and M5 model? Maybe you've learned to tap it sharply once to access the Emoji on your Mac while typing. I use it all the time and wanted to explain why.

While it's not on most third-party keyboards, the Globe key is a fixture on MacBooks such as the latest and greatest M6 and other Apple keyboards. It doubles as the Function (Fn) key, which is why it carries both a globe icon and the letters "Fn." It still works as a Function key: hold it while pressing one of the "F" keys along the top row of the keyboard to trigger their actions, which can include shortcuts on your Mac. Doing so overrides any F key's default system function, such as brightness, volume controls and Spotlight search. In this case, Globe/Fn acts as a modifier key.

If you use F-keys extensively in your work (I'm looking at you, programmers and gamers), you can make them the default behavior. Open Settings > Keyboard and toggle Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys to On. Moving forward, you'll need to press the Globe/Fn button to access brightness and volume controls.
The MacBook Globe key lets you navigate your Mac
Combined with a letter, your little Globe key also helps you in other ways:
• Fn + E: Opens the Emoji and Symbols viewer.
• Fn + D: Starts or stops voice dictation.
• Fn + C: Opens Control Center.
• Fn + N: Opens Notification Center.
• Fn + A: Moves keyboard focus to the Mac icon and activates the Dock.
• Fn + Q: Creates a Quick Note in Notes.

If you see no value in any of those, you can assign the Globe with a more useful task in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Modifier Keys where you use the drop down menu so that a single tap of the Globe icon acts just like the Control, Option, Command, or Escape keys, or No Action.

It's also a Page Up/Down button. Press Globe + Backspace/Delete to perform a forward delete; use Globe and an up or down arrow to scroll one full page at a time; or use it with the left or right arrows to jump to the beginning or end of a document.
If you're multilingual, you may have multiple language keyboards enabled on your Mac. A quick press of the globe key lets you seamlessly switch between them.
You can customize what a single tap does in Settings > Keyboard > Press Globe key to. The dropdown menu lets you set it to Change Input Source, Show Emoji & Symbols, Start Dictation, or Do Nothing.
How to use the Globe key like a pro

When working on a MacBook, the Globe key comes into its own for the window tiling functions it unlocks. These are useful on any display, but they prove invaluable when working across multiple apps on a smaller screen.
• Globe + Control + Arrow keys: Snap the active window to the top, left, bottom or right of the screen.
• Globe + Control + Shift + Arrow keys: Tile the active window to one half of the display while automatically placing the second most recently used window in the opposite half.
• Globe + Control + Option + Shift + Arrow key: Arrange three windows with one window taking up half the space.
• Globe + Control + F: Expand the active window to fill the whole desktop, but not in full-screen mode.
• Globe + Control + C: Center the active window on screen or use R instead of C to return the window to its previous dimensions.

Finally, the little globe keyboard character helps navigate the desktop. Globe + F toggles full-screen on and off, while Globe + H moves open windows aside. Tap Globe + M to move keyboard focus to the top menu bar, allowing users to navigate app menu items using the arrow keys. Press Globe + Control + F8 to focus on the status icons on the right of the menu, or use Globe + Shift + A to open or close the App Browser. With all these useful talents provided by the confusing little Globe key, it might be time to start using it more often.

nytimes.com/2026/11/28/world/middleeast/.headline: Netanyahu, Under Pressure, Offers Rival Lead in Unity Government

paragraphs.text: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel said Saturday that his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, could serve first as prime minister in a possible unity government, in what analysts called a last-minute attempt to stave off being removed from power.

Political analysts said Mr. Netanyahu’s apparent concession reflected the growing pressure he now faces as his opponents gather momentum to replace him. But they said it was still unclear whether Mr. Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff who made Mr. Netanyahu’s ouster the centerpiece of his campaign, could keep his fractious bloc together.

Mr. Netanyahu’s offer quickly divided the prime minister’s opponents, underscoring how Mr. Eisenkot stands at a fateful crossroads in the partners he chooses and rejects. His mandate to form a government is set to expire in about a week, although he can formally request an extension from Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, for up to two weeks if necessary.

While Mr. Netanyahu’s critics hoped the October elections would serve as a reckoning over the prime minister’s leadership, no bloc received a clear majority. Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition received 53 seats in the 120-member Parliament, while Mr. Eisenkot’s supporters got 48. Soaring turnout among Israel’s Arab minority delivered their parties a combined 19 seats.

Mr. Eisenkot could choose to partner with Arab parties that are widely viewed by Jewish Israelis as insufficiently Zionist. He could try to ally with ultra-Orthodox parties reviled by many of his voters. Or he could join up with Mr. Netanyahu, extending a political lifeline to a man he repeatedly has said is unfit to lead.

Since the election, Mr. Netanyahu has overseen racially charged attacks against the Arab parties, which he claimed were masterminding the “Islamization of Israel.” He has also asserted that Arab parties stole the vote, claiming with little evidence that the results were tainted in an effort reminiscent of President Trump’s 2020 “Stop the Steal” campaign.

On Saturday night, Mr. Netanyahu offered Mr. Eisenkot a coalition in which both men would serve as prime minister, going further than previous unity proposals. Mr. Eisenkot would serve first, with Mr. Netanyahu serving “at the beginning of the term as alternate prime minister,” he said in a statement.

Mr. Netanyahu said that his concession aimed to avert the “existential threat” of the Arab parties’ gaining power. If that happened, he said, “Without firing a single bullet, hostile elements will take control of the country from within.”

A unity government between Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party and his rivals could create a stable parliamentary majority — which Mr. Eisenkot has struggled to find so far. But it would go against Mr. Eisenkot’s campaign promise to unseat Mr. Netanyahu’s government.

Mr. Eisenkot will probably also be wary of Mr. Netanyahu’s offer given what happened in 2020, when Benny Gantz, another former military chief of staff, joined Mr. Netanyahu in a unity government. Mr. Gantz was supposed to be prime minister second, after Mr. Netanyahu — who dissolved Parliament before his rival got a turn in the top spot.

Mr. Eisenkot is expected to meet with Mr. Netanyahu on Sunday morning just north of Tel Aviv for negotiations, according to representatives for both leaders. It would be the first known formal meeting between the two men since the last month’s indecisive Israeli elections.

The prospect of Mr. Netanyahu’s remaining in government divided his opponents. Many of Mr. Eisenkot’s supporters rejected the offer outright. Yair Golan, who leads the left-wing Democrats party, denounced what he called Mr. Netanyahu’s “stunts and tricks,” calling for an immediate “government of change and salvation.”

Naftali Bennett, who leads the 12-seat Together party, called for Mr. Eisenkot to negotiate with Mr. Netanyahu, whom he praised as “doing the right thing.” But his faction’s co-founder, Yair Lapid, called Mr. Netanyahu’s offer a “transparent scam by a serial fraudster.”

This past week, it seemed that Mr. Eisenkot was pushing toward forming a government made up of Mr. Netanyahu’s rivals, with support from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties. He finalized coalition agreements with the Democrats as well as the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party, both of which bitterly oppose Mr. Netanyahu.

One major hurdle was whether Mr. Eisenkot could bring in support from the Arab parties without losing support from right-wing parties. Mr. Eisenkot had also set a condition for those parties to join an Israeli coalition, saying they must denounce Hamas as a terrorist organization, which neither had officially done.

On Saturday night, Mansour Abbas, the head of Raam — the single largest Arab party — appeared to try to clear the hurdle. In an interview with Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster, Mr. Abbas said that his party had signed onto a bill in Parliament that included language defining Hamas as a terrorist organization.
Asked by the interviewer to clarify his position, Mr. Abbas pointed to the bill. “You see the bill?” he said. “What’s written is written — that Hamas is a terrorist group.”

Mr. Abbas, like other Arab leaders, has unequivocally condemned the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel — the deadliest day in the country’s history — which killed about 1,200 people and triggered the devastating war in Gaza. He has also called for Hamas to disarm in accordance with President Trump’s cease-fire plan.

But Israel’s Arab parties had hesitated to label Hamas a terrorist organization officially, a fundamental belief for most Jewish Israelis. While Palestinians are deeply divided over Hamas’s actions, many view armed struggle in general as legitimate resistance to Israeli rule.

Mr. Abbas said he had delayed taking the stance in part because he did not want it to serve as a justification for “total war” against Palestinians. But it was unclear whether his statement on Saturday would satisfy Mr. Eisenkot’s condition.

nytimes.com/2026/11/28/nyregion/macys-th.headline: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Hits 100 (Give or Take a Couple of Days)

paragraphs.text: It was a centennial celebration 102 years, and two days, in the making.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, a mainstay of the holiday, set off under a bluish sky Saturday for the 100th time in its history — and for the first time on a day other than Thanksgiving, after weather delayed the event by two days.

The event was postponed late on Wednesday after forecasters predicted extreme winds and inclement weather in New York City, upending plans for thousands of would-be spectators, visitors and performers.
The decision was among only a handful of occasions when the procession’s schedule has been altered, chief among them World War II, when a helium shortage led to a three-year hiatus.

But on Saturday, the rescheduled parade went off with few hitches, as hundreds of thousands of people thronged the sidewalks of Upper and Midtown Manhattan to catch a glimpse of glittering floats and bobbing balloons, and many more tuned in to the broadcast at home.

The scene was somewhat mellower than past years, some spectators said, as the festivities coincided with holiday shopping and long weekend sojourns. Still, the sidewalks bustled from early morning till noon as the parade snaked its way down the center of Manhattan.

There was Gloria Gaynor, JoJo and the casts of several hit Broadway shows belting songs and twirling along. There were youth marching bands, who remained in the city against the odds, tooting horns and clapping cymbals. And there was Smash Mouth, Baha Men and the Indigo Girls, playing their hits to elated crowds as Pikachu, Smokey Bear and Snoopy soared overhead.

By the end, the parade showcased some 30 giant balloons, 28 floats, eight marching bands and dozens of performers, Macy’s said, though at least a few groups originally scheduled to perform, including the University of Alabama’s marching band and Macy’s Great American Marching Band were forced to skip their shows after the delay.
For others, though, the Saturday step-off afforded the chance of a lifetime: a front-row seat to the parade’s 100th procession.
“It feels festive in a more general way,” said Destinee Filmore, who came to the parade route from Harlem because of the delay. “It feels more like a holiday.”
Nate Schweber, Miles G. Cohen, Sarah Maslin Nir and Mack Liederman contributed reporting.

sports.yahoo.com/college-football/articl.headline: Ohio State vs Michigan recap: Buckeyes win 45-0 in The Game

paragraphs.text: Well, that was more like it.

Ohio State beat Michigan 45-0 on Saturday at Ohio Stadium, closing the regular season the way the rivalry demands — with a record, a breakout running back, and a brawl for good measure. It was the largest margin of victory in the history of The Game, and the first time the Buckeyes have shut out Michigan since 1962.

The Buckeyes are 8-4 now, 6-3 in the Big Ten, and they finish the regular season on the highest of notes. Michigan falls to 6-6, 3-6 in the conference. There was no Big Ten title or College Football Playoff berth on the line in this one. There was only The Game, and Ohio State took it in front of 105,708 fans.
Ohio State vs Michigan: How the Buckeyes won it

Ohio State wasted no time. The Buckeyes took the opening kickoff, and after a Michigan personal foul gave them the ball at their own 40, they marched 60 yards in six plays. Luke Fahey hit three big passes on the drive, found Bo Jackson on an 18-yard pass to the Michigan one, and Jackson punched it in from a yard out with 11:32 left in the first quarter. Ohio State 7, Michigan 0.

The second quarter belonged to Jeremiah Smith. After Michigan missed a 30-yard field goal, Ohio State put together a 13-play, 80-yard drive that took 6:48 off the clock, and Fahey found Smith for a five-yard touchdown with 13:29 left in the half. It was Smith's first catch of the game, his 18th receiving touchdown of the season — breaking Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record of 17, set in 1995 — and he struck the Heisman pose in the end zone. It was also the first time since 1995 that Ohio State scored on its first two drives of The Game. Ohio State 14, Michigan 0.

Jackson struck again with 5:22 left in the half, taking a handoff on the first play of the drive and running 29 yards through a facemask penalty for his second touchdown of the day. Ohio State 21, Michigan 0, and that was the halftime score.

The second half was more of the same. Connor Hawkins' 32-yard field goal with 8:25 left in the third quarter, capping a nearly six-minute drive, made it 24-0. Michigan's best drive of the day ended on downs when Qua Russaw sacked Bryce Underwood on fourth-and-8 with 4:14 left in the quarter. Then Jackson completed his hat trick with an eight-yard touchdown run with 1:13 left in the third, finishing an eight-play, 72-yard drive. Ohio State 31, Michigan 0 after three quarters.

Smith added two more in the fourth. He caught a two-yard touchdown with 9:00 left — an 11-play, 49-yard drive — to tie Desmond Howard's Big Ten single-season record of 19. Ohio State 38, Michigan 0. Michigan's one would-be score, a 70-yard fumble return by Aisea Moa, was wiped out on review. Then, after an offensive pass interference call erased one touchdown catch, Smith hauled in a pass on fourth-and-13 with 1:45 left for his third touchdown of the day and his 20th of the season, breaking Howard's record outright. Ohio State 45, Michigan 0, and that was the final.
Bo Jackson and Jeremiah Smith lead Ohio State vs Michigan
If there is a one-line version of this game, it is Jackson and Smith.

Jackson was the workhorse with Ja'Kobi Jackson out, and he ran like it all afternoon: 24 carries for 170 yards and three touchdowns, plus three catches for 69 yards — 239 yards from scrimmage in the game of his career. He scored the first touchdown of the game and the one that made it a three-score game, and he did it running through contact both times. Jackson is now the second Buckeye ever to rush for 1,000 yards as a freshman and a sophomore, joining J.K. Dobbins.

Smith did not need many touches to make history. His first catch of the game was the record-breaker, and he finished with eight catches for 90 yards and three touchdowns. That gave him 94 catches and 1,572 yards for the season, with 20 touchdowns — breaking Glenn's Ohio State record and Howard's Big Ten record. He finished one catch short of Jaxon Smith-Njigba's single-season record of 95, and 34 yards short of Smith-Njigba's 1,606.

Fahey, the true freshman starting with Julian Sayin out for the season with a fractured elbow, was calm from the start and finished 18 of 36 for 253 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Along the way, he broke Terrelle Pryor's record for passing yards in a season by a true freshman.
Ohio State defense shuts down Michigan
The defense that had given up 30-plus points in three of its last four games held Michigan to 150 total yards and kept the Wolverines off the scoreboard.

Bryce Underwood, cleared to start after being listed as questionable all week with a lower-body injury, never got comfortable. He finished 9 of 17 for 86 yards with an interception, and the Buckeyes sacked him three times, two of them by Khary Wilder. Jaylen McClain had the interception. Michigan managed seven first downs all day, and its only real scoring chance was the missed 30-yard field goal on its opening drive.

Ohio State outgained Michigan 484-150, held the ball for 35:21, and went 6-for-6 in the red zone. It was the Buckeyes' tenth shutout of Michigan all time, and the first shutout in the rivalry since Michigan beat Ohio State 28-0 in 1993.
What Ohio State's win over Michigan means
First, the bowl picture. The Buckeyes will learn their bowl destination on Dec. 6, with the Citrus Bowl, ReliaQuest Bowl and Music City Bowl among the possibilities.

Second, Ryan Day. He came into the day 2-4 against Michigan, with both wins coming in Ann Arbor and no win over the Wolverines in Columbus. Now he has his first home win in the rivalry, Ohio State's first win over Michigan in the Shoe since 2018, and the Buckeyes' first back-to-back wins over Michigan since the eight-game winning streak that ended in 2019. Day is now 3-4 in The Game.

Third, Smith. He got the biggest record on his first catch of the afternoon, then broke the Big Ten record for good measure. He finished one catch and 34 yards short of Smith-Njigba's single-season records — marks that will stand unless he plays in the bowl game.
Contact/Follow us @BuckeyesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Ohio State news, notes, and opinion. Follow Phil Harrison on X: @PhilHarrisonBW.

sports.yahoo.com/nascar/articles/ryan-bl.headline: Ryan Blaney’s 94-Point Gap Was Pure Bad Luck

paragraphs.text: Ryan Blaney had a career year in 2026 and still lost the crown by a razor-thin margin. With a gap of just 94 points, he was once again on the verge of securing a NASCAR Cup Series championship. He finished fourth in the standings, just behind champion Kyle Larson. This tiny gap came after Blaney earned his fourth win of the season, tying a career-high mark. He also secured his 21st career win overall. Per Yahoo Sports, this was his third top-five points finish in the last five seasons.

Blaney set new personal bests for laps led with 1,107 and top-10 finishes with 23. He also claimed five poles, the most in his career. His average finish of 12.7 was his best in a NextGen Cup season. Yet, four bad races in the final stretch undid all that hard work. In the final 10 races, four results of 33rd place or lower cost Blaney the title. Each of those disasters happened when he had a real shot at a top-10 spot.
The Three Races That Cost a Title

Three specific crashes at three different tracks wiped out his title hopes. Although Blaney placed fourth in every stage at Gateway, his final position was 35th. A blown brake rotor caused the issue, a problem NASCAR fixed the very next week. That single bad finish cost him at least 31 points he would have likely gained. Then came Bristol, where Blaney was running second before Carson Hocevar put him into the wall. Even a third-place finish there would have given him another 31 points. Hocevar later fought with Blaney on pit road, but the damage to the points was already done.

The final blow happened at Martinsville. Josh Berry brake-checked Blaney, ruining his chances for an eighth-place stage finish and ending his race. Berry went on to finish fourth. If Blaney had posted a comparable result, he would have lost those stage points, and the margin needed to beat Larson would have risen above 94 points. These three incidents alone cost him well over 100 points. The new format demands consistency every single week, and Blaney simply could not get it in the final 10 races.
2027 Looks Different With a New Car

Blaney does not need to hang his head over this loss. He had a career-high season that proved he can win four races in a row. The Ford team is already looking ahead with a new body design. The new Ford body offers superior turning capability in traffic and enhanced overall performance. Blaney will be the face of that new car in 2027. He might be the next driver pictured next to the Bill France Cup. The 94-point gap was a matter of bad luck, not a lack of speed.
Louisville Cardinals (6-1) vs. Creighton Bluejays (7-1)
Players Era Festival 16 Championship
Game Time: 10:30 p.m.
Location: Michelob ULTRA Arena: Las Vegas, Nev.
Television: ESPN
Announcers: Dan Shulman (play-by-play) and Jay Bilas (analyst)
Favorite: Louisville by 6.5
Series: Creighton leads, 3-1
Last Meeting: Creighton won 89-75 on March 20, 2025 in the NCAA Tournament first round in Lexington, Ky.
Series History:
Projected Starting Lineups:
• G Jackson Shelstad (6-1, 185, Sr.)
• G Adrian Wooley (6-4, 205, Jr.)
• F Karter Knox (6-6, 220, Jr.)
• F Alvaro Folgueiras (6-10, 230, Sr.)
• F Flory Bidunga (6-9, 235, Jr.)
• G Wes Enis (6-1, 200, Sr.)
• G BJ Davis (6-1, 175, Sr.)
• G Austin Swartz (6-4, 205, Jr.)
• F Jackson McAndrew 6-10, 235, Jr.)
• F Oswin Erhunmwunse (6-10, 240, Jr.)
Statistics:
Creighton’s Season to Date:
Relevant Videos:
About Creighton:

A team that many people thought would go 0-3 in Las Vegas, Creighton instead comes into Saturday night’s Players Era championship game riding a five-game winning streak and looking to continue its early-season resurgence under first-year head coach Alan Huss.

The Bluejays are 7-1 after an impressive run in Vegas that has included wins over Michigan, TCU and No. 22 Gonzaga. Those triumphs, coupled with a neutral court win over Iowa, have helped erase the sting of an 89-82 road loss to a not great Kansas State team.

Named the replacement to longtime head coach Greg McDermott last March, Huss — a Creighton player from 1997-2001 — spent six seasons as an assistant with McDermott from 2017-23 before returning as associate head coach in 2025. He also spent two seasons as the head coach at High Point, compiling a 56-15 record and leading the Panthers to the NCAA Tournament in 2025. His teams at High Point were known for their offensive production, and he inherits a Creighton program that has traditionally been one of the better offensive teams in the country. One of the biggest areas of emphasis under Huss has been creating a more disruptive defensive identity, using length, pressure and activity to force turnovers and make life difficult for opposing offenses.

The biggest offensive weapon for the Bluejays is a player Louisville fans should be familiar with in senior guard Wes Enis. The 6-1 transfer from South Florida is averaging 19.4 points per game and leads the team with 33 made three-pointers.

Enis is the son of former NFL running back and Penn State All-American Curtis Enis, and he has an interesting background beyond that. A self-described “zero-star prospect” coming out of high school in Ohio, Enis took college-credit courses and graduated early from Miami East High School, sacrificing the chance to play his senior season of high school ball. Instead, he enrolled early at Division-II Lincoln Memorial in December of 2023. His intention all along was to prove himself and earn a shot at the D-I level.

Enis scored 1,002 points in just two seasons at Lincoln Memorial, averaging over 20 points per game in his sophomore season. That same year he earned conference Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year honors, while also drawing interest from a litany of respected D-I programs. He chose USF, and immediately became the team’s standout scorer in his first and only season with the Bulls.

When he’s on, Enis is just about as dangerous an outside shooter as there is in the country. He isn’t exceptionally quick with the ball in his hands, but he’s quick enough. His handles and his effective twitchiness allowed him to get to the rim consistently against most American Conference defenders, and he’s a crafty finisher once he get there. Enis is also the best mid-range player on the team, and he’s really good at doing that slight arm extension thing (read: uncalled offensive foul) to create space before taking a 10-15 footer.

Enis has been particularly productive during Creighton’s run through the Players Era tournament, scoring 24 against Michigan, 20 against TCU and 28 against Gonzaga. He’s coming into Saturday’s game playing some of the best basketball of his career. He also likely has a chip on his shoulder after declaring before last season’s first round game against Louisville that South Florida was “the better team,” and then proceeding to 2-for-15 from the field and 0-for-11 from three against the Cards.

The other major backcourt weapon for Creighton is BJ Davis, a 6-foot-1 senior transfer from San Diego State. Davis is averaging 16.9 points per game and has been one of the most versatile players on the roster. He’s capable of scoring from the perimeter, attacking the basket and creating opportunities for his teammates. He put together an extraordinary performance in Friday night’s win over Gonzaga, recording 27 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists for a triple-double. Davis also scored 10 points in overtime, helping the Bluejays pull away after trailing by eight points late in regulation. He’s quickly become one of the most important players on Huss’s roster.

Austin Swartz (8.9 ppg) provides another experienced option in the backcourt. The 6-foot-4 junior can knock down outside shots, handle the basketball and contribute as a secondary playmaker. Freshman Katrelle Harmon (5.6 ppg) has also been an important contributor, particularly as a facilitator. His ability to distribute the basketball gives Huss another option when Davis isn’t initiating the offense. Hudson Greer has provided additional scoring off the bench and is another player capable of hurting opponents from beyond the arc.

Up front, Creighton has an interesting combination of size, athleticism and versatility. Jackson McAndrew, a 6-foot-10 forward, is an especially intriguing player because of his ability to stretch the floor. McAndrew, who I believe is the only primary contributor for Creighton who played in the tournament game against Louisville two years ago, is comfortable operating away from the basket and can create matchup problems for opposing big men. Oswin Erhunmwunse provides a more traditional interior presence, bringing size, rebounding and athleticism around the rim. The Bluejays also have Fredrick King, a 6-foot-10 senior who contributed nine points and nine rebounds in Friday’s win over Gonzaga. Freshman Trevon Carter-Givens gives Huss another big body to work with, while Jasen Green provides additional frontcourt experience and versatility.

One of the most interesting things about this Creighton team is how quickly it has developed an offensive identity under Huss. The Bluejays are averaging 86.3 points per game through eight contests and shooting 37.8% from three-point range. They’ve scored at least 95 points in each of their last three games, including the overtime win against Gonzaga Friday night. They also do a good job sharing the basketball, averaging nearly 18 assists per game. Enis and Davis are the primary scoring options, but Swartz, McAndrew and Greer give them additional players capable of making opponents pay for focusing too much attention on the two leading guards.

Defensively, Huss is trying to establish a more aggressive identity than Creighton has traditionally been known for. The Bluejays are averaging more than 11 steals per game and have forced opponents into considerably more turnovers than they’ve committed themselves. They’re holding opponents to 42.8% shooting from the field and 32.3% from three-point range. The combination of Davis’s perimeter defense, the length of the frontcourt and Huss’s emphasis on creating pressure has helped produce some encouraging early results.

This is a team that can really score out of an offense that is still very similar to the one that torched Louisville two seasons ago. Enis is the player who can get hot in a hurry, while Davis is capable of hurting opponents in several different ways. The Cardinals need to make both players work for their points, avoid allowing easy transition opportunities and keep Creighton’s supporting cast from getting comfortable. Davis’s playmaking ability also makes it important to avoid overcommitting defensively and giving him easy opportunities to find open teammates.

Louisville should also have opportunities to attack Creighton inside and use its athleticism around the basket. The Bluejays have some size, but their offense is driven primarily by their guards, and making them defend physically for 40 minutes should be an important part of the game plan.
